sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Chris Berube, sitting in for Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是克里斯·贝鲁比，代班罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Back in January, about 10 million people tuned into the hockey romance series Heated Rivalry.
sentences.zh: 早在今年一月，大约有一千万人收看了冰球浪漫剧集《炽热宿敌》。

sentences.en: Even I watched it, because the show is made in Canada by Canadians, and I'm Canadian.
sentences.zh: 连我都看了，因为这部剧是加拿大人在加拿大制作的，而我就是加拿大人。

sentences.en: And the Canadian-ness, it's kind of everywhere.
sentences.zh: 那种加拿大特色，可以说是无处不在。

sentences.en: The main characters in the show go to a cottage at one point, not a cabin.
sentences.zh: 剧中的主角们在一集里去了一个度假屋（cottage），而不是小木屋（cabin）。

sentences.en: One of the hockey studs has an interview with a journalist in pretty passable high school French.
sentences.zh: 其中一位冰球帅哥用相当过关的高中法语接受了一名记者的采访。

sentences.en: Look, it's all there in the text.
But if you ask me, the most Canadian part of the series is the music.
sentences.zh: 但如果你问我，这部剧最具加拿大特色的是什么，那就是音乐。

sentences.en: That's producer and fellow Canuck, Max Collins.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人兼同胞马克斯·柯林斯。

sentences.en: The soundtrack is loaded with artists from Canada.
sentences.zh: 原声带里全是来自加拿大的艺术家。

sentences.en: There's needle drops of songs by Feist and the Soul Jazz Orchestra and Dilly Dally.
sentences.zh: 里面有Feist、Soul Jazz Orchestra和Dilly Dally的歌曲插播。
对我来说，这太令人高兴了。

sentences.en: But the Canadian music wasn't obvious to everyone watching.
sentences.zh: 但并不是每个看剧的人都能一眼听出其中的加拿大音乐。

sentences.en: I found this out when I threw on the show with my roommate, Key.
sentences.zh: 我是和室友Key一起看这部剧时发现这一点的。

sentences.en: Can I ask if you've ever been with another guy?
sentences.zh: 我能问你以前有没有和另一个男生在一起过吗？

sentences.en: Key knew and loved a lot of the songs Unheated Rivalry.
sentences.zh: Key认识并喜欢《炽热宿敌》中的很多歌曲。

sentences.en: Like this power ballad by the band Wolf Parade.
sentences.zh: 比如这首来自Wolf Parade乐队的力量抒情曲。

sentences.en: The song plays during the emotional climax of an episode,
sentences.zh: 这首歌在一集的情感高潮部分响起，

sentences.en: when a closeted hockey player invites his boyfriend out to center ice for the first time, and they kiss.
sentences.zh: 当时一名隐柜冰球运动员第一次邀请他的男朋友来到冰场中央，然后他们接吻了。

sentences.en: But Key isn't originally from Canada, and they weren't aware that Wolf Parade is from Montreal.
sentences.zh: 但Key并不是土生土长的加拿大人，他们也不知道Wolf Parade来自蒙特利尔。

sentences.en: Actually, Key was shocked to hear that a lot of the big musicians they know are Canadians.
sentences.zh: 事实上，Key听到他们知道的很多大牌音乐人都是加拿大人时，感到十分震惊。

sentences.en: Oh, I did not know Deadmau5 was Canadian.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不知道Deadmau5是加拿大人。

sentences.en: Okay, maybe you're thinking, Wolf Parade's Canadian.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许你在想，Wolf Parade是加拿大人。
当然，这有什么大不了的？
对我们加拿大人来说，这很重要。

sentences.en: If you are American and you have Canadian friends,
sentences.zh: 如果你是美国人，而且有加拿大朋友，

sentences.en: perhaps you've noticed that any time a Canadian celebrity is mentioned,
sentences.zh: 你或许会注意到，每当提到某个加拿大名人时，

sentences.en: people like me love to point it out.
sentences.zh: 像我这样的人总是忍不住要指出来。

sentences.en: Look, we just cannot help ourselves.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们就是控制不住自己。

sentences.en: Oh, did you know that Mac DeMarco is from Canada?
sentences.zh: 哦，你知道Mac DeMarco来自加拿大吗？

sentences.en: Part of the reason this game is so fun for us is because of the sheer volume of secretly Canadian artists.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得这个游戏这么有趣，部分原因在于这些秘密具有加拿大背景的艺术家数量实在太庞大了。

sentences.en: Sure, everybody knows Drake and Justin Bieber are from Canada,
sentences.zh: 当然，人人都知道Drake和贾斯汀·比伯来自加拿大，

sentences.en: but when you start to dig in, we are literally everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但当你开始深入挖掘时，就会发现我们简直无处不在。

sentences.en: We're responsible for Nelly Furtado and Pup and Kay Trinata and Propagandhi.
sentences.zh: Nelly Furtado、Pup、Kay Tranita和Propagandhi都是我们培养出来的。

sentences.en: This is just a small sample of an overwhelming liSt.
sentences.zh: 这只是那长得吓人的名单中的一小部分。

sentences.en: Canada is a country with about 41 million people.
sentences.zh: 加拿大是一个拥有约4100万人口的国家。

sentences.en: That's only a little bit bigger than the population of California.
sentences.zh: 这只比加利福尼亚州的人口稍微多一点。

sentences.en: But the country punches well above its weight in terms of very famous musicians.
sentences.zh: 但就知名音乐人的数量而言，这个国家的影响力远超其体量。

sentences.en: 50 years ago, Canada's music industry was basically non-existent.
sentences.zh: 50年前，加拿大的音乐产业基本上可以说是名存实亡。

sentences.en: And the most successful Canadian musicians were expats making it big in the United States.
sentences.zh: 最成功的加拿大音乐人都是去美国大获成功的侨民。

sentences.en: But today, Canada has one of the biggest music industries in the world.
sentences.zh: 但今天，加拿大拥有世界上规模最大的音乐产业之一。

sentences.en: And it's partly thanks to some good old-fashioned government meddling.
sentences.zh: 这部分要归功于一些老式的政府干预。

sentences.en: It's a public policy that was really controversial, but it's been imitated all over the world.
sentences.zh: 这是一项曾引发巨大争议的公共政策，但后来被世界各地争相效仿。

sentences.en: I'm talking about a policy called CanCon.
sentences.zh: 我说的就是被称为CanCon的政策。

sentences.en: Okay, so, to understand this policy, we got to rewind to just before the dawn of Canada's music boom,
sentences.zh: 好吧，要理解这项政策，我们得把时间倒回到加拿大音乐大繁荣前夕，

sentences.en: In those days, most of the stuff played on Canadian radio was produced outside of Canada.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，加拿大电台播放的大多数歌曲都不是在加拿大制作的。

sentences.en: The biggest musicians at the time were mostly from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当时最大的音乐人大多来自美国

sentences.en: places with a bunch of recording studios to produce music,
sentences.zh: 那些地方有大量用于制作音乐的录音室，

sentences.en: and a bunch of record labels to distribute it,
sentences.zh: 有大量用于发行的唱片公司，

sentences.en: and a bunch of radio stations to market it,
sentences.zh: 有大量用于营销的广播电台，

sentences.en: and a lot of fans to consume it.
sentences.zh: 还有大量的粉丝来消费音乐。

sentences.en: But Canada, on the other hand, had pretty much none of that.
sentences.zh: 但相比之下，加拿大几乎什么都没有。

sentences.en: If you were a Canadian musician, there was essentially no modern music industry.
sentences.zh: 如果你是个加拿大音乐人，基本上就不存在什么现代音乐产业。

sentences.en: Alan Cross is a radio legend in Canada,
sentences.zh: 艾伦·克罗斯是加拿大的广播传奇人物，

sentences.en: and host of a long-running documentary series called The Ongoing History of New Music.
sentences.zh: 也是长寿纪录片系列《新音乐的不断演变的历史》的主持人。

sentences.en: Back then, there was very little in the way of development, nurturing, coaching, mentoring of Canadian talent.
sentences.zh: 当时，在发掘、培养、执教、辅导加拿大本土人才方面，几乎是一片空白。

sentences.en: I was just like, you know, get out there and play.
sentences.zh: 我当时的想法就是，你知道的，走出去演出吧。

sentences.en: Record labels in Canada were mainly set up to distribute American records domestically.
sentences.zh: 加拿大的唱片公司主要是为了在国内发行美国唱片而设立的。

sentences.en: And on top of all that, there was a stereotype that Canadian music was somehow inferior.
sentences.zh: 最要命的是，当时有一种成见，认为加拿大音乐在某种程度上低人一等。

sentences.en: Canadian radio stations had this thing that Canadian music was substandard or not popular
sentences.zh: 加拿大的广播电台有一种看法，认为加拿大音乐不合格、不受欢迎，

sentences.en: or had no potential, no commercial or ratings appeal.
sentences.zh: 或者没有潜力，没有商业价值或收视率吸引力。
艾伦在这里并没有夸大其词。

sentences.en: Another Canadian music industry legend, Stan Cleese, saw this bias firsthand.
sentences.zh: 另一位加拿大音乐产业传奇人物斯坦·克利斯曾亲眼目睹这种偏见。

sentences.en: Here's Cleese recounting an experience he had in an interview with music historian Kenneth Murphy.
sentences.zh: 这里是克利斯在接受音乐历史学家肯尼斯·墨菲采访时回忆的一段经历。

sentences.en: The guy opened the little envelopes that they got from the record companies,
sentences.zh: 那家伙打开了他们从唱片公司收到的信封，

sentences.en: he looked at it, and he said,
Canadian shit threw it against a cement brow qual and it shattered and fell to a fall.
sentences.zh: 加拿大的垃圾，然后把它狠狠摔在水泥墙上，碎落一地。

sentences.en: The thinking was, you're just not good enough.
sentences.zh: 当时的观点是，你们就是不够优秀。

sentences.en: If we put your song next to the Beatles or the Rolling Stones
sentences.zh: 如果我们把你们的歌和披头士、滚石乐队

sentences.en: or any of the other music coming out of the United States, it would sound bad.
sentences.zh: 或其他任何来自美国的音乐放在一起，听起来就会很糟糕。

sentences.en: It did not meet the standards, which may have been unfair and prejudicial, but that was the attitude.
sentences.zh: 它不符合标准，这可能很不公平且带有偏见，但当时的态度就是这样。

sentences.en: With this lack of infrastructure and this bias against Canadian musicians,
sentences.zh: 由于缺乏基础设施以及对加拿大音乐人的这种偏见，

sentences.en: there were two paths you can take to become a Canadian hitmaker.
sentences.zh: 你当时有两条路可以成为加拿大的热门歌手。

sentences.en: Path one, leave Canada for more fertile musical soil.
sentences.zh: 第一条路，离开加拿大，去音乐土壤更肥沃的地方。

sentences.en: This was the path taken by some of our most notable folk musicians at the time,
sentences.zh: 我们当时一些最著名的民谣音乐人就是走的这条路，

sentences.en: like Leonard Cohen, who moved out to New York City,
sentences.zh: 比如搬到纽约市的伦纳德·科恩，

sentences.en: or Neil Young, who went out to Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 或是前往洛杉矶的尼尔·杨。

sentences.en: For those who couldn't make the move abroad,
sentences.zh: 对于那些无法出国发展

sentences.en: and those who didn't want to,
sentences.zh: 以及不想出国的人来说，

sentences.en: Ride the coattails of the British Invasion, baby.
sentences.zh: 那就是借着英国入侵的东风，宝贝。

sentences.en: Some bands would slap a Union Jack on their instruments,
sentences.zh: 有些乐队会在乐器上贴上英国国旗，

sentences.en: and others would fraudulently write things like
sentences.zh: 还有些乐队则会在巡演海报上厚颜无耻地写上

sentences.en: England's number one group on their tour posters.
Jack London and the Sparrows took it a step further.
sentences.zh: 杰克·伦敦与麻雀乐队则走得更远。

sentences.en: While their front man was from the UK,
sentences.zh: 虽然他们的主唱来自英国，

sentences.en: the rest of the band was Canadian and put on fake English accents.
sentences.zh: 但乐队其余成员都是加拿大人，却装出了假英国口音。

sentences.en: In a similar fashion, a Winnipeg garage rock band,
sentences.zh: 用类似的方式，温尼伯的一支车库摇滚乐队，

sentences.en: formerly known as Chad Allen and the Expressions,
sentences.zh: 也就是以前的乍得·艾伦与表达乐队，

sentences.en: obscured their origins to trick Canadian radio stations
sentences.zh: 掩盖了他们的出身，以此欺骗加拿大广播电台

sentences.en: They had just recorded a cover of Shaken All Over.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚录制了一首《Shaken All Over》的翻唱版。

sentences.en: But in the Canadian music is bad mindset of the mid-60s,
sentences.zh: 但在60年代中期“加拿大音乐不行”的心态下，

sentences.en: this Canadian record had to be fed to radio stations in a sneaky way.
sentences.zh: 这张加拿大的唱片必须偷偷摸摸地塞给广播电台。

sentences.en: So they pressed up a whole bunch of records,
sentences.zh: 于是他们压制了一大批唱片，

sentences.en: and they took them to radio stations across the country,
sentences.zh: 把它们带到全国各地的广播电台，

sentences.en: and they played them this record without telling them who it was.
sentences.zh: 在不告诉对方是谁的情况下播放了这张唱片。

sentences.en: The label only said, guess who?
sentences.zh: 唱片公司只说了一句：猜猜是谁？

sentences.en: And in 1965, it sounded like a British Invasion band,
sentences.zh: 在1965年，这听起来就像一支英国入侵时期的乐队，

sentences.en: and they were, oh, this is really cool.
sentences.zh: 他们当时就觉得，哦，这太酷了。

sentences.en: From then on, the new name stuck,
sentences.zh: 从那以后，这个新名字就被叫开了，

sentences.en: and the guess who went on to write chart-topping classics.
sentences.zh: “猜猜是谁”乐队后来创作出了登顶排行榜的经典之作。

sentences.en: Canada didn't have a strong sense of national pride in the 50s and 60s.
sentences.zh: 在50和60年代，加拿大并没有强烈的民族自豪感。

sentences.en: The music industry was a prime example of this.
sentences.zh: 音乐产业就是这方面的典型例子。

sentences.en: Musicians had to hide their Canadian-ness or move away just to find success in Canadian markets.
sentences.zh: 音乐人不得不隐瞒自己的加拿大身份，或者背井离乡，只为了能在加拿大市场获得成功。

sentences.en: But near the end of the 1960s, Canada had a big surge in national pride.
sentences.zh: 但到了60年代末期，加拿大的民族自豪感迎来了大爆发。
1967年，这个国家迎来了百岁生日，

sentences.en: and the government of Canada was determined to celebrate in style.
sentences.zh: 加拿大政府决心大肆庆祝一番。
各种新音乐节纷纷开办。

sentences.en: There was a months-long cross-country canoe race.
sentences.zh: 还有历时数月的跨国独木舟比赛。
毫无疑问，最盛大的庆祝活动，

sentences.en: the one that captured the attention of the whole world,
sentences.zh: 那个吸引了全世界目光的活动，

sentences.en: Expo 67, the greatest show on Earth.
sentences.zh: 67年世博会，地球上最伟大的表演。

sentences.en: Expo 67 was a world's fair held in Montreal over six months.
sentences.zh: 67年世博会在蒙特利尔举办，历时六个月。

sentences.en: The fair saw 50 million people come through its gates.
sentences.zh: 世博会迎来了5000万名游客。

sentences.en: That's more than twice the entire population of Canada at the time.
sentences.zh: 这比当时加拿大全国总人口的两倍还要多。

sentences.en: It was one of the most successful world exhibitions.
sentences.zh: 这是最成功的世界博览会之一。

sentences.en: And it helped shine an international spotlight on the country at large.
sentences.zh: 它帮助这个国家在国际上大放异彩。

sentences.en: Suddenly, though, Montreal and Canada have found an identity and reputation
sentences.zh: 突然之间，蒙特利尔和加拿大找到了一种身份认同和声誉，

sentences.en: that owes nothing to the paSt.
I think of 1967 as being a bit of a watershed moment.
sentences.zh: 我认为1967年是一个具有分水岭意义的时刻。

sentences.en: Erin McLeod is a music journalist and educator.
sentences.zh: 艾琳·麦克劳德是一名音乐记者兼教育工作者。

sentences.en: Like, all of these things sort of come together as a means of attempting to push forth
sentences.zh: 就像是，所有这些事情汇聚在一起，试图推行

sentences.en: a notion of what it means to be Canadian, you know,
sentences.zh: 一种关于身为加拿大人意味着什么的观念，你知道的，

sentences.en: in the face of, like, the increasing ability of the United States
sentences.zh: 面对的是美国日益强大的文化统治力

sentences.en: to spread its cultural dominance quite literally everywhere.
sentences.zh: 在可以说是每一个角落的蔓延。

sentences.en: Coming out of its centennial year, Canada's national pride had pulled a 180.
sentences.zh: 在经历百年华诞之后，加拿大的民族自豪感发生了180度大转弯。

sentences.en: Canadians had just experienced 12 months of intense patriotism.
sentences.zh: 加拿大人刚刚经历了长达12个月的强烈爱国主义洗礼。

sentences.en: But that sense of pride didn't match up with the state of Canada's cultural landscape.
sentences.zh: 但这种自豪感与加拿大的文化景观现状并不相符。

sentences.en: The music sector was still in rough shape.
sentences.zh: 音乐产业当时依然处境艰难。

sentences.en: Enter our unlikely hero of arts and culture, the Feds.
sentences.zh: 这时，我们意想不到的艺术与文化英雄登场了：联邦政府。

sentences.en: On February 12th, 1970, Canada's cultural regulator, the CRTC,
sentences.zh: 1970年2月12日，加拿大的文化监管机构——加拿大广播电视委员会（CRTC）

sentences.en: proposed some changes to the licensing requirements for all broadcasters.
sentences.zh: 向所有广播公司提出了一些关于牌照要求的新变更。

sentences.en: The goal was to support Canadian musicians and to prop up the industry.
sentences.zh: 其目的是支持加拿大音乐人并扶持整个行业。

sentences.en: And to accomplish this, the CRTC made it mandatory for every Canadian radio station
sentences.zh: 为了实现这一目标，CRTC强制规定每一家加拿大广播电台

sentences.en: to broadcast a certain amount of Canadian music every week.
sentences.zh: 每周必须播放一定数量的加拿大音乐。

sentences.en: This was such a big deal.
cancelled their regular programming that night to talk about it at length.
sentences.zh: 当晚取消了常规节目，对此事进行了长篇大论的讨论。

sentences.en: Good evening, I'm Gordon Donaldson with Normandy Polk.
sentences.zh: 晚上好，我是戈登·唐纳德森，与我同主持的是诺曼迪·波尔克。

sentences.en: Today has been a pretty dramatic one for broadcasting in Canada.
sentences.zh: 对于加拿大的广播界来说，今天是相当戏剧性的一天。

sentences.en: A 30% Canadian content rule for the use of music by radio stations.
sentences.zh: 电台播放音乐时必须有30%的加拿大内容配额。

sentences.en: A 30% mandate for Canadian music on the radio.
sentences.zh: 电台播放的加拿大音乐需达到30%的硬性规定。

sentences.en: These laws became known as Canadian content laws.
sentences.zh: 这些法律后来被称为加拿大内容法。

sentences.en: And the content itself became known as CanCon.
sentences.zh: 而这些内容本身则被称为“加康”（CanCon）。

sentences.en: Now, was Canada the first country in the world to try out something like CanCon?
sentences.zh: 那么，加拿大是世界上第一个尝试类似“加康”这种机制的国家吗？

sentences.en: Australia beat us to the punch in 1942.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚在1942年就抢先一步了。

sentences.en: But their regulations were pretty loose.
sentences.zh: 但他们的规章制度相当松散。

sentences.en: The goals for CanCon regulations were more strict,
sentences.zh: 而“加康”法规的目标则要严格得多，

sentences.en: thanks to a very picky bureaucrat named Pierre Junot.
sentences.zh: 这要归功于一位极其挑剔的官僚皮埃尔·瑞诺。

sentences.en: We believe that there is enough talent in Canada.
sentences.zh: 我们坚信加拿大拥有足够的人才。

sentences.en: It's a matter of making room for the new talents that are developing in Canada.
sentences.zh: 问题在于为加拿大正在崭露头角的新人才腾出空间。

sentences.en: Junot was the chair of the CRTC.
And as the biggest cultural rulemaker,
sentences.zh: 作为最具权势的文化规则制定者，

sentences.en: he was determined to have Canadian music played all the time on the radio.
sentences.zh: 他决心让广播电台时刻播放加拿大音乐。

sentences.en: the CRTC would have to find the answers to some pretty big questions.
sentences.zh: CRTC必须先找到一些重大问题的答案。

sentences.en: Questions like, what makes a piece of music Canadian?
